text: The append is one synchronous operation of rwb-decision on the decision base, POST /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log, called by rwb-agent as the first step of its suggestion transaction with the case reference, the run reference, the treatment reference, the model code, the model version, the inputs snapshot reference, the suggested terms, the decided time and an idempotency key of the form TDR_OFFER:<treatmentId>, and answered 201 with the record reference, the chain sequence, the entry hash and the decided time; the record exists only when the answer returns, and a failure leaves rwb-agent's run without a decision link and returns no suggestion to the treatment. The per-service login is called the rwb-decision login (DP-02) because its name is not given, and the request and answer field set of section 12.1 stays the placeholder until the contract baseline is agreed.
why: TSD P7 v2 T-A.1 documents only the two reads of the ledger and the legacy story writes the entry in process inside the monolith, so the write path of the target has neither a method nor a path nor a body, while rwb-agent has to store a decision reference on its run and the whole suggestion has to be withheld when the record cannot be written.

impact: No business value changes: the code, the model version, the final call, the actions and the chain are the legacy ones. If the append becomes an event or an in-process library call on the caller's side, the call-type summary and one consumed or published row change, and the fail-closed behaviour of AC6 and the one-record rule of AC7 keep their criteria.

text: The decision code D5 and the final call SUGGESTION_RECORDED are values of reference lists read through the reference-data contract of rwb-case with the version in force; D5 is kept as the legacy decision log mapping records it and SUGGESTION_RECORDED is the legacy final call, so neither the code nor the final call is a constant in code and the lists are the only source of their values. A code, a final call or a required version that is not of its list is refused with 422 and MSG-P7-009 naming the field.
why: TSD P7 v2 T3.2 carries no decision code list and no final-call list, and the legacy story writes both as literals of its mapping, so a record cannot be validated or tested without a stated reading of where the values live and which values they are; Template and Rules R3 and DP-07 put reference data with rwb-case.

text: The model code, the model version, the status, the fallback, the guardrail result, the suggested terms, the treatment and case reference and the inputs snapshot reference of the record are taken from the run read of rwb-agent and not from the caller; the inputs reference of the record is that snapshot reference, the recommendation is the suggested terms of the run, agent_version is written null because a model output carries no prompt, and the actions are the treatment reference and the run reference. The field names of that read are the placeholder until RWB-P10-E2032-CON publishes them, and the treatment and case references in the criteria stay the legacy values T-1001 and RW-2026-001001.
why: REQ-DRI-001 and NFR-033 require the record to name the version that produced the recommendation, a caller that sends its own version could misstate it, and the legacy mapping leaves the model version and the inputs reference to be filled from the run.

text: This story has no feature switch of its own: the legacy flag rwb.agent.tdr-suggestion stays with RWB-P10-E2032-APP, it gates the suggestion and the suggestion area of SCR-14 there, and it never gates the append of the record, because a suggestion that reached the model gateway must carry its record or it is a defect and not a degraded mode; the policy mode OFF is a business rule of rwb-agent and not a switch of this service.
why: The legacy story sets one flag for the whole capability and the target splits the capability across two services, so the flag has to be placed, and placing it on the record path would let a configuration change create an unrecorded suggestion.
